A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MRMR benchmark. Their main text, figures, tables and complete Appendices A–G support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval evaluations in Tables 3 and 7, qualitative error analyses, and query-expansion experiments in Table 8.

after.justification: v2 reports revised retrieval evaluations, an original annotation-quality audit, additional error cases and expanded query-expansion experiments in Tables 8–10.

M1.justification: The task formulations, benchmark-construction workflow, four retrieval approaches and query-expansion procedure remain the same. Newly supplied prompts and annotation descriptions document procedures without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 23-domain coverage and Knowledge, Theorem and Contradiction tasks, including Negation, Vehicle Design and Traffic Case. The smaller Theorem sample changes evaluation composition rather than domain or task coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparison retains the same 14 models. However, Appendix F.3 adds Ops-MM-Embedding to the query-expansion comparison previously conducted only with GME-Qwen2-VL, using the same two expansion models.

E3.justification: The Theorem evaluation is substantively revised: Table 2 reduces its queries from 579 to 512 and changes positive-document statistics, including Business from 2.2 to 3.2 positives per query. Section 5.1 changes the case review from 20 queries with top-5 documents to 30 with top-10. The new annotation audit checks 120 documents per task. Metrics and corpus sizes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds a quantitative false-positive/false-negative audit and four Theorem error cases covering geometry, statics, thermodynamics and data interpretation. Query-expansion analysis now tests a stronger retriever and exposes a harmful expansion setting. The existing Agriculture and Traffic illustrations are retained.

E5.justification: Table 8 newly estimates annotation-error prevalence from sampled documents, reporting explicit 120-document denominators and false-positive/false-negative counts and proportions for Knowledge and Theorem. Neither version provides confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 3 substantially revises Theorem scores and overall averages: Qwen3-Embedding changes from 52.1 to 54.1 and merged-image GME-Qwen2-VL from 25.3 to 36.2. These accompany a revised evaluation set, not demonstrated same-setting improvements. GME query-expansion gains change from 16.5/26.5 to 5.1/14.8. New Ops-MM-Embedding results show its average changing from 52.4 without expansion to 48.5 with the smaller expansion model and 54.3 with the larger one.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same mathematical retrieval formulation and relevance definitions. No new theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations are introduced; formulas in examples and error discussions illustrate benchmark questions.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain expert-domain, reasoning-intensive, interleaved multimodal retrieval and the Contradiction task. The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims that caption-assisted text retrieval performs best and multimodal retrievers struggle with reasoning. Updated counts and scores do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix F.3 qualifies query-expansion benefits: expansion quality becomes critical for stronger retrievers, and weaker-model expansions can hurt. New Theorem cases explain failures involving geometric constraints, procedural knowledge and numerical interpretation. Appendix F.1 also adds an interpretation that the observed annotation-error rates support benchmark reliability.

D1.justification: v2 adds four construction prompts, an evaluation-code access link, cross-query annotation details, source-license information and clarification that Negation construction uses no LLM prompting. These materially expand reproducibility documentation. Conversely, v1's Appendix C.4 disclosure of expert spot-checking 20% of added Wikipedia content and download/OCR error handling is removed.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to existing retrieval benchmarks and methods remain unchanged. Correcting the source description to MMMU-Pro and adding a URL to the existing Qwen3-Embedding reference do not introduce new research positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are preserved. Local changes include the expanded ethics statement, acknowledgments, affiliation and conference-header updates, wording corrections, and appendix subsections for prompts and expanded analyses.

P2.justification: v2 adds four prompt figures and two analysis tables, relocates existing appendix displays and supplies a sharper Negation illustration. Existing benchmark diagrams, annotation screenshots and data examples are otherwise retained. The overall visual design and main-table structures remain stable.

improvement.justification: The construction prompts, evaluation-code link, annotation audit and stronger-retriever expansion experiment modestly improve reproducibility and evidential support. The gains are limited by unexplained Theorem sample and relevance-statistic revisions and removal of the earlier spot-check disclosure. v2 also introduces a reporting error: Table 3 gives VLM2Vec an average of 18.1 although its 11 displayed scores average 16.6.
